content: {"rule": "K-G4", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "This judge text decides whether verses on the cited-in line count as unanswered witnesses and whether the broken link is retracted, which is what K-G4 governs.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "the line is cured by retraction, not defended: every witness pressed against C3 was named and answered in the challenger's own later rounds ((DR2) §C and (DR3) C3 quoting Matthew 1:18, 1:25 and Deuteronomy 22:24; (DR3) C4 quoting Luke 1:34), so the \"witness left unanswered\" ground fails and the collision is regraded UNDERDETERMINED; with that retraction the challenger's standing is corrected to SELF-SUPPORTED (L=6, c=0, no link BROKEN)", "rule_words": "A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.", "room": "I interpreted 'A verse the judge says was answered is not counted' and 'A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way': I weighed (1) the judge's statement that the witnesses were answered and that there is 'no link BROKEN' means they are not counted, so no quoted pressed sentence is needed, versus (2) the earlier 'CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN' line counts them toward a broken link, so K-G4 would require a quoted pressed sentence and named round.", "why": "The judge text says the witnesses were answered/retracted and that no link is BROKEN, so under K-G4 they are not counted as unanswered and no quoted pressed sentence is required."}
